The image shows soybean leaves with white, powdery patches scattered across the upper leaf surface. The coating appears as small white patches that are beginning to coalesce. The leaf texture underneath looks normal (green, no necrosis or angular lesions). This is a classic presentation of Powdery Mildew — white powdery fungal growth on the leaf surface, exactly matching the description of "white, powdery coating on leaves that begins as small patches and coalesces to cover entire leaves."

No evidence of angular lesions (rules out Bacterial_Blight), no brown spots or pustules (rules out Septoria, Rust, Bacterial_Pustule), no vein necrosis, no tan/brown lesions with colored margins.
